question: What are two reasons to create an Application instead of an Integration Project? (Choose two.) A. When multiple subflows are required B. When more than one message flow is required C. When creating a schema is required D. When referencing static libraries are required E. When referencing a shared library is required
discussion: Selected Answer: CE Correct Answer: CE Explanation: An application can contain schema files, which are used to define the structure and format of data that flows through a message flow. An integration project cannot create schema files, only reference them from an application or library. An application can reference a shared library, which is a collection of resources that can be reused by multiple applications. A shared library can contain message flows, subflows, Java code, ESQL modules, and other artifacts. An integration project can only reference a static library, which is a collection of resources that are copied into the integration project at design time. upvoted 2 times Submit Cancel
